# Missionaries and cannibals: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `missionaries-and-cannibals.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.39) and `missionaries-and-cannibals-rules.soar` (32 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_river.py`). Needs Soar 9.6.6.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . missionaries-and-cannibals.soar --seed 1 --cap 300000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . missionaries-and-cannibals.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py missionaries-and-cannibals init-mac.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

World: init-mac.world (two banks; three missionaries, three cannibals and the boat on the first bank).

## Results (Soar 9.6.6, 16 Nov 2026)

Plans were replayed independently by `check_plan.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`) | fail-mac: goal false, failure true; final-mac: goal true, failure false; init-mac: goal false, failure false; init-mac2: goal false, failure false. All as the instructor intended. |
| Seeds 1-3, library v2.39, init-mac2 | solved: 5 crossings on every seed, 1,655 / 1,585 / 1,262 decisions |
| Seed 1, library v2.39, three missionaries and three cannibals (init-mac) | not solved: no move within 300,000 decisions; with `^iterative-step tie-impasse`, 2 legal crossings |
| Seed 1, library v2.37, init-mac, no control on real moves | not solved: 18 crossings in 300,000 decisions (333 with tie-impasse) |

## Translation

- Operators: ferry-one ("the boat and a block on the current bank onto the opposite bank"; argument1 = the block, argument2 = the opposite bank) and ferry-two ("a block ... and another block ... and the boat"; argument1 and argument2 = the two blocks, the lower ^index first; the destination is the opposite bank). Each operator records the bank it leaves (^from), so its look-ahead application fires once.
- current is expanded in place (a bank below the boat); opposite is a maintained one-argument relation.
- The goal ("all the blocks are on a destination bank") is expanded over the blocks of the world file (the boat is a block).
- "the number of cannibals (missionaries) on a bank" is a maintained attribute ^cannibal-count (^missionary-count) of each bank, changed by every crossing.
- The losing condition is read with the usual exception (A-M1): a bank with cannibals and no missionaries is safe.
- "The solution has five steps." does not match this world (11 crossings): reported, not used.
- Search control added at JL's direction (16 Nov 2026), not from the English: in look-ahead, a move whose result is a situation already on the current look-ahead path is rejected. A situation is the bank of every block; each operator carries the label of the situation it produces (^result), the task object the label of the current one (^situation), and the look-ahead application records both on the history object (^visited). Real moves (JL, 16 Nov 2026, as in mc-world): a real move back to a situation already visited is worst (the top state records ^real-visited).

## Assumption ledger

| ID | Statements | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| A-R1 | 9 | "a block ... and another block": two different blocks, neither the boat; each pair is proposed once (lower ^index first). |
| A-M1 | 12 | A bank with cannibals and no missionaries is safe (the usual reading). Read literally ("more cannibals than missionaries"), the puzzle has no solution. |
| A-M2 | 12 | "the number of cannibals (missionaries) on a bank" is a maintained attribute of each bank, changed by every crossing. |
| A-C1 | all | "all the blocks" is expanded over the blocks of the world file (the boat is a block), so the goal test is positive. |
| A-C2 | all | "current" is expanded in place; "opposite" tests absence and decides legality, so it is a maintained one-argument relation. |
| A-C3 | all | "The solution has N steps." is checked against the plans, not used. |
| S-1 | (JL) | Search control, not from the English (16 Nov 2026): in look-ahead, a move whose result is a situation already on the look-ahead path is rejected. |
| S-2 | (JL) | Search control, not from the English (16 Nov 2026, as in Tasks/From-English/mc-world): a real move back to a situation already visited is worst. |
